construct: With the first breaths, pulmonary vascular resistance falls and pulmonary blood flow increases. Increased pulmonary venous return raises left-atrial pressure above right-atrial pressure, pressing the septum primum against the septum secundum and functionally closing the foramen ovale.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: After the first breaths, pulmonary vascular resistance falls and pulmonary blood flow rises; increased pulmonary venous return raises left-atrial pressure above right-atrial pressure, pressing septum primum against septum secundum and functionally closing the foramen ovale.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Ductus-arteriosus constriction is a real postnatal event but does not directly close the foramen ovale. Pulmonary vascular resistance rises in fetal life and falls after birth; umbilical venous return stops, and placental removal raises rather than lowers systemic resistance.
